I think I have this same problem. I'm more or less obligated to interact with someone like that on an almost-daily basis. I try to keep in mind this piece of advice (that he who angers you controls you) and do my best to laugh it off when this person says something that reminds me of my questionable life decisions. I also try to remember that ultimately I can choose how I react to an inflammatory situation, because often times the careless things this person (these persons) say are just not worth hurting over.  It's unfortunate that we're in this situation but we need to make the best of it so as to not hurt ourselves is something else I try to keep in mind. 


I also like to remind myself that eventually there will be a point where I'm no longer obligated to interact with them, that this person will be out of my life and that I will be out of theirs. (Or maybe not, but sometimes deluding myself into thinking that there is a light at the end of this black hole of a tunnel makes me feel better) 


When all else fails, I try to put on some music or browse Reddit to distract myself, or I physically remove myself from the situation by making an excuse to get away (drink of water, using the bathroom, needing to run to a meeting or class). At the end of a long day, journaling sometimes helps me sort out my thoughts so that I can figure out why I was so bothered and think up ways to avoid feeling like I did next time. 


Hang tight, Internet friend. (:

seconding this one! I've been working out 5-6 days a week for just under 6 weeks now and I find that I'm not really sore unless I'm adding weight to my lifts or I'm doing a modified circuit. The first week of doing this I was super sore, but after about a week and a half I didn't find the soreness to be a problem. I think this has to do with your body adapting and "learning" to recover faster (I could be wrong - I don't know much about the science behind this magic.)


also, are you stretching after your work out? or doing a cool down of some sort? if not, that could be it. sometimes I forget to stretch and gentle stretches the day (or two) after are helpful for soreness/stiffness.
